base.note: first parent of the introducing commit

introducing_commit.subject: fix(evals): compact Pi JSON transport
introducing_commit.size: code 141 lines in 5 files (evaluate.mjs 10, pi-adapter.mjs 28, plan.mjs 13, process.mjs 86, semantic.mjs 4) plus 3 test files; under the 250-line limit, whole change used

exclusion_reason: documentation and references are not code or tests

real.defect: retain() increases retainedOutputBytes before checking it against outputLimitBytes (the check is on line 46). A chunk that is rejected is still counted, so retained_output_bytes overstates what was kept and can exceed the limit.
real.consequence: The evidence's retained_output_bytes is inexact. In the probe, 10 bytes were kept but 20 were reported against a limit of 15.

proof.kind: fix commit's test failing on the introducing state
proof.command: node --test --test-name-pattern="retained byte accounting" .skill-eval/evaluate-skill/tests/process.test.mjs (fix-state process.test.mjs, run on the introducing state)
proof.result_introducing: not ok 1 'retained byte accounting includes only evidence actually appended': expected 10, actual 20
proof.result_fixed: pass (fix commit and the control state)
proof.intro_suite: real: node --test process, pi-adapter, plan => 14 pass, 0 fail

real.second_real_behaviour_not_used: The same fix also stops observeTransport from setting output_limit_exceeded when raw transport overflows. The introducing commit's own test asserts the old behaviour, so this is treated as a design change and not as part of this defect. The fix's process test file also fails on the introducing state for that reason, and it is not used here.

seeded.defect: Seed: the newline condition is inverted in the transformed-line retain call. Lines that were terminated lose their newline, and the final unterminated line gains one.
seeded.base_state: Introducing change with the counter corrected as the fix corrected it (process.mjs retain: check first, then add, then count) and the seed applied. Other files and the committed tests are the introducing commit's versions.

proof.kind: committed test that passes on control and fails on seeded
proof.control: base + seeded files with the seed reverted (process.mjs line 71 back to terminated ? "\n" : "")
proof.result_seeded: 13 pass, 1 fail: 'not ok 13 retained output limit ignores compacted cumulative transport bytes' (line count 100 expected)
